key_insight: V-Retrver turns multimodal retrieval from passive, language-driven reranking into an agentic, evidence-driven loop where the model actively verifies fine-grained visual evidence—reducing speculative reasoning in ambiguous cases and improving candidate selection.
problem_solved: Current MLLM-based retrieval methods rely on static visual encodings and CoT-style language reasoning without actively checking visual evidence, which causes hallucination and poor reranking on visually ambiguous or detail-sensitive queries.
method: Reformulate retrieval as an agentic evidence-gathering and verification process: the model iteratively requests and inspects fine-grained visual evidence tied to retrieval candidates.
Combine chain-of-thought style reasoning with active visual grounding to validate or refute candidate matches rather than relying solely on language priors.
Score and rerank candidates using integrated multimodal evidence (visual cues + reasoning trace) to produce more reliable retrieval decisions.
impact: This approach makes multimodal retrieval more robust and interpretable by grounding decisions in verifiable visual evidence—helpful for developers building retrieval systems, VQA, and any application where minimizing hallucination and improving fine-grained accuracy matters.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram of the agentic loop: candidate set → visual evidence queries → grounded reasoning → reranking.

Bar chart or precision/recall illustration (schematic) showing qualitative improvement in reranking reliability and interpretability.
paper_title: V-Retrver: Evidence-Driven Agentic Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Retrieval
paper_authors: Dongyang Chen, Chaoyang Wang, Dezhao SU, Xi Xiao, Zeyu Zhang
